By the Court:- Heard the parties.

2.  This Criminal Miscellaneous Petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with a prayer to quash and set aside the entire criminal proceeding arising out of Jamshedpur Cyber P.S. Case No.30 of 2022 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 66C & 66D of the Informant Technology Act including the charge sheet and cognizance order dated 28.06.2022 in connection with the said case against the petitioner.
3.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

The brief facts of the case is that huge amount of money of several lakhs was withdrawn by committing fraud by the petitioner and the co- accused persons by cloning the cheque of the informant, while the ( 2025:JHHC:26820 ) original cheque is with the informant and the specific role played by the petitioner in the said offence is of activating the sim card, having the same sim number as that of the husband of the informant, which was registered with the bank and the same Md. entities.text: Anwar Ali vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the investigation of the case, the complicity of the petitioner was found and police submitted charge sheet inter alia against the petitioner for having committed the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B/34 of the Indian Penal Code and the learned Special Judge, Cyber Crime, Jamshedpur upon submission of the charge sheet took cognizance of the said offences vide order dated 28.06.2022.
4. Learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is innocent and has not committed any offence.

It is next submitted that the petitioner has activated the sim card of the husband of the informant on the documents relating to the same being produced by someone,
hence, no illegality has been committed by him nor there is any laches on the part of the petitioner.
It is next submitted that the defrauded amount of the informant has been deposited back in the account of the husband of the informant by the Punjab National Bank.
It is lastly submitted that the prayer, as prayed for in the instant Cr.M.P, be allowed.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the State on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer of the petitioner made in the instant Cr.M.P and submits that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner that the petitioner in criminal conspiracy with the co-accused person has forged the Aadhar Card of the husband of the informant and ( 2025:JHHC:26820 ) activated the sim bearing same sim number, as that of the husband of the informant, which was registered with the joint account of the informant with her husband with Punjab National Bank and the petitioner was also instrumental in issuance of the forged duplicate cheque for committing the crime.
It is lastly submitted that this Cr.M.P., being without any merit, be dismissed.

6. Having heard the rival submissions made at the Bar and after carefully going through the materials available in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that there is direct allegation against the petitioner that, with the complicity of the petitioner, forging of the Aadhar Card of the deceased husband of the informant and by using such forged Aadhar Card as a genuine one, activating of the sim card bearing the same number, which was registered with the bank account of the husband of the informant, was done fraudulently.
Further, cybercrime of swindling away the huge amount of money from the account of the husband of the informant has been done by cloning the cheque, with the active involvement of the petitioner.

So, this Court is of the considered view, that the allegations against the petitioner is sufficient to constitute the offences in respect of which cognizance has been taken by the learned Special Judge (Cyber Crime), Jamshedpur against the petitioner also, for having committed the said offences in criminal conspiracy with the co- accused persons.

Therefore,
this Court is of the considered view that there is no justifiable reason to accede to the prayer made in this Cr.M.P. to quash and set aside the entire criminal proceeding arising out of Jamshedpur Cyber P.S. Case No.30 of 2022 registered for the offences ( 2025:JHHC:26820 ) punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 66C & 66D of the Informant Technology Act including the charge sheet and cognizance order dated 28.06.2022 in connection with the said case against the petitioner; in exercise of its power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
7.
Accordingly, this Cr.M.P. being without any merit, is dismissed.
